limitations: 功能摘要根据作者固定版本材料归纳，不是逐字引文或独立效果验证。

evidence.summary: 核查 README.md、package.json、entry.js、src/client.js、src/boot-screen.js、src/screensaver.js、src/idle-probe.js、src/renderers.js、src/remux.js、tools/install.sh、tools/uninstall.sh、LICENSE、cordis.patch.yml；[Q01](#research-q01)、[Q02](#research-q02) Host 注入独立脚本并提供媒体/设置路由，client 激活通知驱动启动交接；屏保以系统闲置或窗口失焦触发，点击或按键退出。
limitations: 固定版本仓库根组件，核查 README、package.json、Host 注入与路由、client 激活、boot-screen 交接、screensaver 触发/退出/清理、idle-probe、renderers、remux 和 shell 安装卸载；非全仓审计。
只执行本工程的统计和结构验证；没有执行目标插件、测试、安装或真实宿主验收。
GitHub/npm 活跃度只作采集背景，未核实独立用户采用或同条件收益对照。

findings.text: [Q01](#research-q01)、[Q04](#research-q04) 面向明确希望个性化 DSH 启动与闲置画面的用户。合格结果是展示结束或手动收回后能继续原任务，收益属于个人视觉偏好。
[Q01](#research-q01)、[Q02](#research-q02) Host 注入独立脚本并提供媒体/设置路由，client 激活通知驱动启动交接；屏保以系统闲置或窗口失焦触发，点击或按键退出。
固定版本仓库根组件，核查 README、package.json、Host 注入与路由、client 激活、boot-screen 交接、screensaver 触发/退出/清理、idle-probe、renderers、remux 和 shell 安装卸载；非全仓审计。
package.json v0.3.0 导出 entry.js 与 ./client，dsh.bundle.patch 指向 cordis.patch.yml，属于原生 DSH 插件；未核实 npm 发布包与提交对应。
[Q03](#research-q03) 的依赖表区分宿主、schema、媒体、Windows 探测、Live2D 和素材权利；不将安装成功视为兼容通过。
[Q03](#research-q03) 的成本表按首次、持续、恢复与退出分开，现金与资源、人工与时间分别记录，量化成本未知。
[Q04](#research-q04) 先确认 DSH/Chromium/schema 条件并备份 profile，用自有短视频关闭声音、开启一次点击进入，保持屏保关闭且不点优化，核对按键与慢启动能放行。再单独验证屏保；误遮挡、不能退出或资源负担明显时关闭两个开关并刷新，按原安装方式撤销。不要将屏保用于敏感会话保护。
[Q04](#research-q04) 的效果表区分已接线机制与未验证体验、可靠性和效率；没有同条件运行收益。
[Q01](#research-q01)、[Q02](#research-q02) 首帧和播放调用结果分开、媒体 renderer 与覆盖层生命周期解耦值得借鉴；移植代价是重接 DOM 进度、激活通知、可见性和系统闲置。[Q03](#research-q03) 同名媒体备份替换是明确取舍，不能当作版本归档。
[Q01](#research-q01)、[Q02](#research-q02) 把预框架启动交接、可选素材和独立页面屏保组合为无需修改 DSH 源码的插件；显式区分首帧、媒体结束与客户端通知，有受控跳过路径。
[Q01](#research-q01)、[Q03](#research-q03) 装饰是否增加不必要等待与维护？15 秒只提示，默认首击可能只解音；屏保非锁屏，非 Windows 触发降级。素材优化会写盘并覆盖同名备份，宿主与资源实际成本未测。
[Q04](#research-q04) 未验证方向是在已有诊断和提示基础上，将客户端激活、素材仍播与可跳过并列解释，并明确首击解音含义；以同场景用户误判、额外等待和干扰对照检验，无改善即否定。

technical.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01) entry.js:1623-1683 将成熟全屏素材与 DSH 注入结合，novelty 为25%常规适配，超过未增量0但无新交互范式支撑50%；boot-screen.js:606-621、1314-1326 的双条件/首帧守卫属于成熟机制的25%适配，尚不足50%突破关键约束。 [Q02](#research-q02) renderers.js:265-309 与显式dispose可在相似宿主迁移，transferability取50%，超过局部25%但仍需重接宿主不达75%；两套生命周期和媒体维护只给 simplification 25%，未证明相对更简单且同等能力的组合足够50%。

business.rationale: [Q04](#research-q04) 对照原生页与系统屏保，未改变任务组织责任，workflow取0%；视觉交接与应用内闲置画面改变呈现产物，delivery取25%，超过无增量但不足50%改变工作交付；[Q03](#research-q03) README:23-29、安装与许可要求没有降低目标人群进入门槛的证据，reach未识别增量取0%，没有新经济组织或资源模式，economics取0%，不能把未测费用记为节省。

recommendation.reason: 明确希望个性化启动与闲置画面、能回滚 profile 的 DSH 本地用户可先用自有短视频、静音和一次点击进入做小范围试用。它把素材选择、交接和页面屏保接入应用内设置，比保留原生启动页多了可配置的视觉呈现，实际等待与资源收益尚未测量。出现放行无效、屏保误遮挡或占用不可接受时，用户应关闭两个开关并刷新，必要时撤销安装行和链接，敏感会话则使用系统锁屏。

scenario.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)、[Q04](#research-q04) README 自述及 entry.js:1623-1683 支持具体偏好人群与视觉任务，超过0%无对象；没有重复痛点或采用必要性直接依据，取25%即8，未到50%15。

advantage.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01) 注入、首帧超时和双条件交接，[Q02](#research-q02) screensaver.js:503-528 应用内让出及双触发，比仅包装入口的25%6有可解释机制增量；受限于等待、平台和偏好未对照，未达75%19，取50%13。

evidence.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01) Host/client完整通知与放行、[Q02](#research-q02) 闲置/点击链、[Q03](#research-q03) remux.js:324-384副作用可回源，超过仅声明25%6；没有真实浏览器/宿主执行，不足75%19，仅取源码50%13。

cost.rationale: [Q03](#research-q03) tools/uninstall.sh:137-185和独立开关提供可识别退路，超过25%5主要无恢复；schema与profile适配、常驻轮询、Windows子进程、可选改写仍需人工复核，未达75%15负担较轻，取50%10。

publication.summaries.text: 为 DSH 提供可配置的全屏启动动画和闲置屏保，支持视频、图片、动图及外接 Live2D。

items.Host 路由: 提供媒体清单与字节、实时屏保设置、系统闲置读数、可选媒体优化及目录打开。
items.界面: 启动覆盖层、独立页面屏保和插件设置卡。
items.事件监听: 订阅页面注入、客户端激活、焦点、可见性、指针与按键事件。
items.后台: 轮询屏保状态，Windows 可用时读取系统闲置探测进程。

publication.capabilities.table:
| 能力 | 主要用途 | 使用条件与边界 |
|---|---|---|
| 启动动画与交接 | 用自选素材覆盖原生启动页并淡出进入 | 依赖宿主注入与客户端通知，可能增加等待，可按键跳过 |
| 页面屏保 | 闲置或失焦后展示素材并点击/按键收回 | 默认关闭，非系统锁屏；非 Windows 仅失焦触发 |
| 素材池与渲染 | 分别管理片头和屏保的视频/图片/动图 | 需浏览器可解码；Live2D 另需外部适配器 |
| 设置卡与预览 | 调整声音、交接和屏保选项 | 依赖宿主 Config/volatile 接线；启动项通常下次刷新生效 |
| mp4 索引优化 | 将媒体索引前置以供更早读取 | 用户触发写盘、默认100MiB上限，同名旧备份会替换，不改变编码支持 |
| 打开素材目录 | 从设置卡定位本地素材池 | Host 发起系统文件管理器，需信任本地环境 |

publication.advice.text: [Q04](#research-q04) 先确认 DSH/Chromium/schema 条件并备份 profile，用自有短视频关闭声音、开启一次点击进入，保持屏保关闭且不点优化，核对按键与慢启动能放行。再单独验证屏保；误遮挡、不能退出或资源负担明显时关闭两个开关并刷新，按原安装方式撤销。不要将屏保用于敏感会话保护。

        "answer": "它是原生 DSH 插件。Host 的 apply 注册媒体路由，并订阅 webserver/index-inject，依次向 head 写入配置、渲染器、屏保与可选启动脚本。启动开关只控制最后一行，因此关掉启动动画仍可独立保留屏保。相比保留原生加载页，其增量是可选素材和可配置的视听交接，适合明确希望个性化启动体验的用户；代码没有减少内核初始化工作，不能解释为启动加速。\n\n自动交接同时受素材完成与本插件 clientReady 通知约束。client apply 先尝试通知覆盖层，再接可选配置卡；因此配置卡失败不应阻断这个通知。clientReady 的事实是本插件客户端入口已激活，不能当成所有工具和业务页面均可操作的验收。进度显示和失败识别另依赖原生 [data-dsh-boot] 元素、进度 CSS 属性及两段英文错误文案，宿主变动会使观察路径失效。\n\n素材清单超过 10 秒未回应时标记素材完成，等待客户端就绪；单项 6 秒无首帧则尝试下一项；未知时长走 20 秒完成路径。15 秒 HOLD 只改提示为“启动较慢，点击继续”，并非强制自动退出。Esc、空格或回车直接调用 enter；默认第一次点击在音频被拦截且有重试函数时只解锁声音，要明确设置 clickToEnter 才把一次点击用作进入。enter 通过淡出后移除覆盖 DOM，交还界面并不证明底层启动成功。\n\n另一个易误解之处是全部素材被禁用时，客户端过滤为空便恢复完整池。用户想完全退出装饰，应关启动总开关并刷新，而不是逐项取消勾选。上述超时与人工放行是有价值的边界控制，但没有真实浏览器故障演练，不能保证所有解码冻结和宿主失败都自动恢复。",

        "answer": "屏保是页面内覆盖层，默认关闭，不是操作系统锁屏或访问控制。触发条件是系统闲置超过阈值，或窗口失焦持续超过阈值，两者任一即可。启动覆盖层仍在时不出现；visibilityState 连续 hidden 满 5 秒时让出，避免瞬时可见性抖动造成闪屏。但别的窗口遮住 DSH 不必然改变 visibilityState，因此不能据此承诺只在真正可见时渲染。\n\n已经出现的屏保由点击或任意按键退出，鼠标移动不退出；tick 没有把系统闲置读数归零当成 dismiss。一次按键会调用 hide(true)，代码本身没有提供密码验证，因此既不适合保护敏感会话，也不应拿它代替系统锁屏。系统闲置值由 Host 侧 Windows PowerShell 长驻子进程调用 GetLastInputInfo 获取；失败有 30 秒退避，读数有 5 秒有效期。其他平台返回不可用并依赖窗口失焦，用户停留在前台长时间不操作的场景并没有同等系统闲置覆盖。\n\n媒体通过统一 renderer 接口呈现，视频有时间线，图片与动图没有可靠结束；Live2D 是可选外部全局适配器，插件不带运行时，缺适配器会报告 no-adapter。屏保能按配置轮换媒体，退出特效与减少动态效果偏好有降级路径。可借鉴的是把媒体生命周期和覆盖层生命周期分开，让 dispose、首帧与结束各表达不同事实；移植仍要重新接实际宿主可见性、媒体策略和焦点事件。\n\n安装函数返回清理定时器、监听和媒体的 disposer，Host 探测器也注册了 dispose。这里确认的是清理实现存在；浏览器脚本卸载时是否总被宿主调用、窗口关闭是否清理 Windows 子进程，都没有本轮运行验收。默认关闭也仍会安装隐藏 DOM、轮询及状态报告，不能宣称关闭屏保即零常驻成本。",

      "content": "# dsh-boot-animation\n\n给 DSH 换掉原生启动页，并给闲置的界面加一层屏保。两个功能各自独立开关，**不改 DSH 本体源码**，升级 DSH 不受影响。\n\n| 功能 | 一句话 |\n|---|---|\n| **启动动画** | 打开页面时用一段全屏短片盖住 DSH 的启动页，片尾交叉溶解进界面。 |\n| **屏保** | 闲置一段时间后用全屏层盖住界面，点一下或按任意键收回，退出时播特效。 |\n\n## 特性\n\n- 素材按扩展名支持四类：视频（`.mp4` `.m4v` `.webm` `.mov`）、静态图（`.png` `.jpg` `.jpeg` `.avif`）、动图（`.gif` `.webp`）、Live2D 模型（含 `.model3.json` 的文件夹）。`.svg` 与 `.mkv` 一律忽略。\n- 片头池多片随机，先把池子里每条轮一遍再重来，不会连着重复同一条；底部进度条跟内核真实的启动进度走。\n- 启动路径上每个走不下去的地方都有上界：素材清单 10 秒不应答就当作没有素材、某段片子 6 秒出不来画面就换下一段、时长未知走 20 秒兜底、内核 15 秒不就绪就提示「启动较慢，点击继续」；Esc / 空格 / 回车随时直接进。\n- 设置全在「设置 → 插件」的「启动动画」卡片里，**不用重启 DSH**：屏保那几项立刻生效，启动动画那几项下次启动生效。\n- 屏保两个触发条件任一满足即出现：整机闲置（Windows 读系统闲置计数）与窗口失去焦点。\n- 屏保收回必须**点一下或按一个键**；鼠标移动不算「回来」，也不会重置窗口失焦的计时（只有 Windows 的整机闲置计数会因为它归零）。\n- 屏保退出三种特效：粒子消散 / 重力下坠 / Glitch 宽带位移，默认每次随机挑一个；关掉是普通淡出。特效是透明的，碎开时露出的是你的界面。\n- 屏保可轮换（15 秒 / 30 秒 / 1 分钟 / 5 分钟，默认不轮换）：到点就换下一条，带交叉溶解，且不会连着放同一条。\n- 不改 DSH 源码：只往 `<head>` 注入脚本，再提供一张设置卡片。\n- 指针互动特效（水波涟漪 / 星屑吸附）的实现仍在代码里，但卡片上**已不提供入口**——这个效果在桌面版上一直没能稳定工作，所以入口被撤了。设置字段与实现都保留，现有配置不会丢。细节见 [MANUAL.md](MANUAL.md)。\n\n## 环境要求\n\n| 条件 | 要求 |\n|---|---|\n| DSH | `0.2.0-rc.2`。这一版换了插件提供设置的接法（声明 `Config`，不再注册命名空间），更旧的 DSH 要用旧版插件 |\n| Node.js | `^22.19.0` 或 `>=24` |\n| 浏览器 | Chromium 内核（Chrome / Edge）。Firefox 没测过 |\n\n## 装法\n\n三条路，选一条。细节与撤销办法见 [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md)。\n\n**路 A：官方命令**\n\n```sh\ndsh plugin --profile web add <解压出来的目录>\n```\n\n这条路会让 pnpm 把依赖也装好，**装完重启一次 DSH**。桌面版（DSH Desktop）的 profile 叫 `desktop`，而这条命令不允许直接改它，桌面版请走路 B 或路 C。\n\n**路 B：Windows 脚本（免重启）**\n\n```powershell\npowershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\\install.ps1\n```\n\n**路 C：macOS / Linux 脚本**\n\n```sh\nsh tools/install.sh --profile desktop   # 桌面版\nsh tools/install.sh                     # dsh web 用的那个（默认 web）\n```\n\n路 B / 路 C 是同一件事：找 DSH 的位置（先看 `DSH_HOME`，再找 `~/.dsh`）、在 profile 的 `node_modules` 里建目录链接、往 `cordis.patch.yml` 追加一行、并把设置卡片需要的 `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`（DSH 自带那份，要 3.18.4 及以上）链上。**不碰 `package.json`，不跑 pnpm。** 找不到 profile 会明确报错并列出有哪些 profile，装之前自动备份 `cordis.patch.yml`；大多数 profile 会热加载，不热加载的脚本会提醒你手动重启。撤销用 `tools/uninstall.ps1` / `tools/uninstall.sh`，参数同上。\n\n> 装完刷新浏览器：看到深海底背景 + 一条短片铺满窗口就是装好了。**左侧菜单里没有「启动动画」这一项**，几乎只有一个原因——插件旁边链接的 `schemastery` 太旧（缺 `.volatile()`），卡片会静默消失，控制台留一条 `boot-animation:` 开头的告警。\n\n## 启动动画\n\n打开页面时依次是：深海底背景 + 一条从片头池随机取来的素材铺满窗口 → 底部一条细进度条跟内核的启动进度走 → 片尾开始溶解进界面 → 覆盖层整个移除。\n\n短片**以静音开始**（Chromium 不允许没有用户手势的带声音自动播放）。点一下画面才开声音，这一下**故意不进入**——手势解锁需要时间起效，绑成一次点击就是「刚出声就进界面」。进入交给片尾；想早点进，点一下或按 Esc / 空格 / 回车。\n\n进入方式三选一：\n\n| 方式 | 什么时候进 | 片子循环 |\n|---|---|---|\n| **片尾交叉溶解**（默认） | 从片尾前「淡入时长」开始溶解，放完那一刻正好进 | 否 |\n| **放完再淡** | 片子完整放完、停住，再淡出 | 否 |\n| **点击才进** | 一直循环播放，直到你点一下 | 是 |\n\n三种方式（「点击才进」除外）都还要等内核就绪——淡入就是界面显形的过程，内核没好就溶解出一个还没搭好的界面。片头放完但内核还没跟上时，画面**停在最后一帧**等它。\n\n退场时片子的声音会和画面一起淡出，不会出现「画面没了声音还在响」或「声音被硬切掉」。地址后面加 `?dshbootdiag=1` 可以让底部提示行变成实时读数（当前素材类型、是否循环、进度与音频状态），用来判断卡在哪一步。\n\n## 屏保\n\n**默认关**，因为它会抢屏幕——默认开着的话，你正在读文档、三分钟没动鼠标，画面会突然被盖住。要用就在设置里自己打开。\n\n**多久算离开**：默认 3 分钟，可选 1 / 3 / 5 / 10 分钟或自定义 1–60 Reporting to the Host\n  // instead means the answer can be read from outside, with nothing asked of the user.\n  // It runs even when the screensaver is switched off, because \"switched off\" is one of\n  // the states worth being able to see.\n  //\n  // Its disposer is KEPT and spliced into the one below: the handle used to be dropped, so an\n  // unload left this interval POSTing the state of a layer that no longer existed.\n  const stopReporting = startStateReporting()\n\n  // `?dshbootdiag=1` additionally turns on an on-screen readout, in the same spirit as\n  // the boot screen's. It also made the\n     * pointer effect unreachable from the card, because the layer came down within a second of\n     * going up.\n     *\n     * So this raises the layer and stops.       "path": "src/idle-probe.js",
      "content": "// System-level idle time, for the screensaver's inactivity trigger.\n//\n// Why the Host half owns this: a renderer can only see input that reaches ITS OWN\n// window. \"Has the user touched the computer at all\" is an operating-system fact, and\n// the OS has been recording it the whole time — `GetLastInputInfo` on Windows, which\n// is what Electron's `powerMonitor` wraps. The plugin cannot reach `powerMonitor`\n// (the desktop app runs the harness as a CHILD Node process, with no Electron\n// bindings), so it reads the same underlying counter directly.\n//\n// How: ONE long-lived child that prints a value on a timer, and a cache this module\n// reads. The alternative — spawning a process per request — costs ~200ms of process\n// creation each time, and this is polled every few seconds; the child costs one\n// syscall per tick (measured at 0.051ms).\n//\n// Nothing here starts until the first read. A profile with the screensaver switched\n// off never asks, so it never pays for a child process, and the child is killed when\n// the plugin unloads.\n//\n// Windows only, and honestly so: `GetLastInputInfo` has no cross-platform twin, and\n// inventing one for macOS/Linux without being able to test it would be a guess\n// presented as a feature. Elsewhere `read()` answers `undefined`, and the screensaver\n// falls back to the window-focus trigger alone — which is a real degradation rather\n// than a silent failure.\n\nimport { spawn, spawnSync } from 'node:child_process'\n\n/**\n * The probe script. Pure ASCII, per this package's rule for generated scripts: the\n * text is piped to PowerShell as a command, and a CJK byte in a comment is enough to\n * break a parser that decodes it as the system code page.\n */\nconst PROBE_SCRIPT = [\n  'Add-Type -TypeDefinition @\"',\n  'using System;',\n  'using System.Runtime.InteropServices;',\n  'public class DshIdleProbe {',\n  '    [StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential)]',\n  '    public struct LASTINPUTINFO { public uint cbSize; public uint dwTime; }',\n  '    [DllImport(\"user32.dll\")]',\n  '    public static extern bool GetLastInputInfo(ref LASTINPUTINFO plii);',\n  '    public static long Ms() {',\n  '        LASTINPUTINFO lii = new LASTINPUTINFO();',\n  '        lii.cbSize = (uint)Marshal.SizeOf(lii);',\n  '        if (!GetLastInputInfo(ref lii)) return -1;',\n  '        return (long)((uint)Environment.TickCount - lii.dwTime);',\n  '    }',\n  '}',\n  '\"@',\n  'while ($true) {',\n  '    Write-Output (\"DSHIDLE \" + [DshIdleProbe]::Ms())',\n  '    Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 1000',\n  '}',\n].join('\\n')\n\n/** How long a reading stays usable. The child ticks every second; this allows for a\n *  few missed ticks before the value is treated as unknown rather than stale. */\nconst READING_TTL_MS = 5000\n\n/** How long to wait for the child to produce its first line before giving up. */\nconst FIRST_LINE_TIMEOUT_MS = 8000\n\n/**\n * How long to wait before trying again after a failure.\n *\n * A failure is rarely permanent — a child can fail to spawn under load, or die hours in —\n * so giving up for the rest of the session is the wrong default. Long enough that a machine\n * which genuinely cannot run the probe is not spawning a process every few seconds, short\n * enough that a transient failure repairs itself within a poll or two.\n */\nconst RETRY_MS = 30000\n\n/**\n * Every probe that has a live child, so process exit can reap them all.\n *\n * The disposer is not guaranteed to run — measured on a real machine, a DSH restart left\n * the previous probe alive holding ~110MB, with a parent pid that no longer existed. So a\n * single exit hook covers every probe in the process, and it is registered ONCE at module\n * load rather than per child: a hook registered per spawn would accumulate one closure per\n * retry, which is a leak of its own.\n */\nconst liveProbes = new Set()\n\nfunction reapAll() {\n  for (const probe of liveProbes) {\n    try {\n      const pid = probe.childPid()\n      if (pid === null) continue\n      if (process.platform === 'win32') {\n        spawnSync('taskkill', ['/pid', String(pid), '/T', '/F'], { stdio: 'ignore', windowsHide: true })\n      }\n    } catch (error) {\n      /* the child may already be gone */\n    }\n  }\n  liveProbes.clear()\n}\n\nif (process.platform === 'win32') {\n  process.once('exit', reapAll)\n}\n\n/**\n * A lazily-started system idle probe.\n *\n * @param options - `{ logger, intervalMs }`. `logger` is the Host context's, used to\n *   report why the probe is unavailable rather than failing silently.\n */\nexport function createIdleProbe(options = {}) {\n  const logger = options.logger\n  const supported = process.platform === 'win32'\n\n  let child = null\n  let buffer = ''\n  let reading = null\n  /**\n   * The reason the probe is PERMANENTLY unavailable — a platform without the API.\n   * Distinct from `lastFailure`, which is a transient reason a retry may clear.\n   */\n  let unavailable = supported ? null : `platform ${process.platform}`\n  /** Why the most recent attempt failed, kept for the diagnostics line. */\n  let lastFailure = null\n  /** When the next attempt is allowed, so a failing probe backs off instead of looping. */\n  let nextAttemptAt = 0\n  let starting = null\n  let disposed = false\n\n  /** Kill the child, if there is one. Safe to call repeatedly. */\n  function stop() {\n    if (child === null) return\n    const dying = child\n    child = null\n    // `kill()` on Windows terminates only the process it names, and PowerShell may have\n    // spawned children of its own. A survivor is not harmless: each one holds ~110MB, and\n    // measured on a real machine two were alive at once — started eight minutes apart,\n    // because a DSH restart did not clean the previous one up. So the whole TREE goes,\n    // and `taskkill /T` is the only reliable way to do that on Windows.\n    try {\n      if (process.platform === 'win32' && typeof dying.pid === 'number') {\n        spawn('taskkill', ['/pid', String(dying.pid), '/T', '/F'], {\n          stdio: 'ignore',\n          windowsHide: true,\n        }).on('error', () => {\n          // If taskkill is unavailable, fall back to the plain kill below.\n          try { dying.kill() } catch (error) { /* already gone */ }\n        })\n      } else {\n        dying.kill()\n      }\n    } catch (error) {\n      /* an already-exited child needs no killing */\n    }\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Start the child, and resolve when it has produced a first reading.\n   *\n   * A failed attempt does NOT latch: `finish(false, ...)` records the reason and\n   * schedules a retry, so a probe that failed once can still come good. Only the\n   * platform check is permanent.\n   */\n  function start() {\n    if (starting !== null) return starting\n    // A failure schedules the next attempt rather than forbidding it.\n    if (Date.now() < nextAttemptAt) return Promise.resolve(false)\n    // Any previous child must be gone before a new one is spawned. Measured on a real\n    // machine: two probe children alive at once, started sixteen minutes apart, 203MB\n    // between them. A retry that spawns without reaping leaves the old process running\n    // forever — it holds a pipe nobody reads and a timer nobody stops.\n    stop()\n    starting = new Promise((resolve) => {\n      let settled = false\n      const finish = (ok, why) => {\n        if (settled) return\n        settled = true\n        if (ok) {\n          // A success clears both the failure record and the backoff, so the probe\n          // reports 'ok' rather than remembering a failure that is over.\n          lastFailure = null\n          nextAttemptAt = 0\n        } else {\n          lastFailure = why\n          stop()\n          nextAttemptAt = Date.now() + RETRY_MS\n        }\n        resolve(ok)\n      }\n\n      let spawned\n      try {\n        spawned = spawn('powershell', [\n          '-NoProfile',\n          '-NonInteractive',\n          '-ExecutionPolicy', 'Bypass',\n          '-Command', PROBE_SCRIPT,\n        ], {\n          // Piped stdout is the point: the values arrive on it. stderr is captured\n          // so a PowerShell parse error can be reported instead of looking like a\n          // probe that simply never answers.\n          stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],\n          windowsHide: true,\n        })\n      } catch (error) {\n        finish(false, `spawn failed: ${String(error.message)}`)\n        return\n      }\n\n      child = spawned\n      let stderr = ''\n\n\n      spawned.stdout.setEncoding('utf8')\n      spawned.stdout.on('data', (chunk) => {\n        buffer += chunk\n        let index\n        while ((index = buffer.indexOf('\\n')) !== -1) {\n          const line = buffer.slice(0, index).trim()\n          buffer = buffer.slice(index + 1)\n          if (!line.startsWith('DSHIDLE ')) continue\n          const value = Number(line.slice('DSHIDLE '.length))\n          if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0) continue\n          reading = { idleMs: value, at: Date.now() }\n          finish(true)\n        }\n      })\n\n      spawned.stderr.setEncoding('utf8')\n      spawned.stderr.on('data', (chunk) => {\n        stderr = (stderr + chunk).slice(-2000)\n      })\n\n      spawned.on('error', (error) => {\n        finish(false, `child error: ${String(error.message)}`)\n      })\n      spawned.on('exit', (code) => {\n        // An exit before the first reading is a failure; an exit later is the child\n        // dying under us, which makes the cached value stale rather than wrong.\n        if (reading === null) {\n          finish(false, `exited early (code ${String(code)})${stderr ? ': ' + stderr.trim().slice(0, 300) : ''}`)\n          return\n        }\n        child = null\n        // A child that dies AFTER working is not a permanent verdict, and treating it\n        // as one is a real bug this used to have: `unavailable` was never cleared, so\n        // one crash — at startup, or hours in — disabled the OS half of the trigger for\n        // the rest of the session. The screensaver then depended on the window-focus\n        // half alone, which never fires for somebody who stays in DSH, so it silently\n        // stopped appearing altogether. `lastFailure` records why, and `nextAttemptAt`\n        // makes the retry a backoff rather than a spawn storm.\n        lastFailure = `child exited (code ${String(code)})`\n        unavailable = null\n        reading = null\n        starting = null\n        nextAttemptAt = Date.now() + RETRY_MS\n        logger?.warn?.(`boot-animation: idle probe exited (code ${String(code)}); retrying in `\n          + Math.round(RETRY_MS / 1000) + 's')\n      })\n\n      setTimeout(() => {\n        finish(false, stderr ? `no reading; ${stderr.trim().slice(0, 300)}` : 'no reading within 8s')\n      }, FIRST_LINE_TIMEOUT_MS).unref?.()\n    })\n    // Cleared once settled, so a retry after the backoff creates a fresh attempt\n    // instead of re-awaiting the promise from the attempt that already failed.\n    starting.then(() => { starting = null })\n    return starting\n  }\n\n  const handle = {\n    /**\n     * The system idle time in milliseconds, or `undefined` when it cannot be known.\n     *\n     * Never throws and never blocks: a caller that polls this on a timer gets an\n     * answer immediately, and an unavailable probe degrades the screensaver to its\n     * focus trigger rather than stalling anything.\n     */\n    read() {\n      if (disposed) return undefined\n      if (!supported) return undefined\n      if (reading === null) {\n        // Kick the start off and answer \"not yet\". The caller polls, so the next\n        // tick gets the value. `start()` itself refuses while the backoff is running,\n        // so this is also what makes a failed probe try again once the wait is over.\n        void start()\n        return undefined\n      }\n      if (Date.now() - reading.at > READING_TTL_MS) {\n        // The value went stale, which means the child stopped reporting. Ask for a\n        // restart rather than serving a reading that no longer describes anything.\n        if (child === null) void start()\n        return undefined\n      }\n      return reading.idleMs\n    },\n\n    /**\n     * What state the probe is in, as one of three values.\n     *\n     * The distinction matters to a caller: `starting` means \"ask again shortly\",\n     * while `unavailable` means \"this will never work here, use the fallback\". Both\n     * make `read()` answer undefined, so a caller that only sees the value cannot\n     * tell a slow start from a permanent failure — and would either give up too early\n     * or keep polling a probe that is never going to answer.\n     *\n     * Only a platform without the API is `unavailable` for good. A failed attempt is\n     * reported as `starting`, because that is what it is: a retry is already scheduled\n     * and may well succeed. Reporting it as `unavailable` would tell the caller to give\n     * up on a probe that is about to come back.\n     *\n     * @returns 'ok' | 'starting' | 'unavailable'.\n     */\n    status() {\n      if (disposed || !supported) return 'unavailable'\n      if (reading !== null && Date.now() - reading.at <= READING_TTL_MS) return 'ok'\n      return unavailable === null ? 'starting' : 'unavailable'\n    },\n\n    /**\n     * Why the probe is not answering.\n     *\n     * `reason` is the PERMANENT verdict (a platform without the API) and is null while\n     * the probe is working, starting, or merely between retries. `failure` is the most\n     * recent attempt's error and is what a diagnostics line wants, since \"it failed and\n     * will retry\" and \"it can never work\" are different answers to the same question.\n     */\n    unavailableReason() {\n      return unavailable\n    },\n\n    /** The most recent transient failure, or null. */\n    failureReason() {\n      return lastFailure\n    },\n\n    /** When the next attempt is allowed, for the diagnostics line. */\n    nextAttemptIn() {\n      return Math.max(0, nextAttemptAt - Date.now())\n    },\n\n    /** Whether a child is currently running. */\n    running() {\n      return child !== null\n    },\n\n    /**\n     * The child's process id, so a leaked one can be found and cleaned up.\n     *\n     * Exposed because the disposer is not guaranteed to run: measured on a real machine,\n     * a DSH restart left the previous probe alive, holding ~110MB. This is what lets a\n     * supervisor notice and reap it.\n     */\n    childPid() {\n      return child === null ? null : child.pid ?? null\n    },\n\n    /** Stop the child. Registered as a disposer so unloading the plugin cleans up. */\n    dispose() {\n      disposed = true\n      stop()\n      liveProbes.delete(handle)\n    },\n  }\n\n  // Registered so a process exit that never runs disposers still reaps the child. See\n  // `liveProbes` for why that is necessary rather than belt-and-braces.\n  liveProbes.add(handle)\n  return handle\n}\n"

      "content": "// Media renderers for the pre-boot screen.\n//\n// The screen used to be video-only: it built a <video>, called play() on it, and\n// read `duration`/`ended`/`volume` off the element. Every one of those is a video\n// fact, and the screensaver has to show still images, animated images and Live2D\n// models through the same overlay. Rather than teach every call site to ask \"what\n// kind is this\", the screen now asks a RENDERER, and this file is where the\n// per-kind knowledge lives.\n//\n// A renderer is a small object with one required method and several optional\n// ones. The contract is deliberately narrow, because everything the screen does\n// with media is one of these questions:\n//\n//   el()            the DOM node to put in the stage                (required)\n//   start()         begin playing / show it                          (required)\n//   dispose()       release everything this renderer created          (required)\n//   onShown(fn)     report that a picture exists (not that play() resolved)\n//   onEnded(fn)     report that it finished; absent = it never ends\n//   duration()      total length in seconds; absent/Infinity = unknowable\n//   currentTime()   playback position in seconds\n//   hasAudio()      whether a sound affordance is worth offering\n//   setVolume(v)    ramp the level; absent = no audio path at all\n//   mute(bool)      silence it without touching level\n//   isMuted()       whether it is currently silent\n//\n// The three timeline questions are answered by ABSENCE, and that is the whole\n// design: a still image has no `duration` and no `onEnded`, so the screen's\n// existing \"unknown length\" path bounds it in time, which is exactly right for\n// something that would otherwise sit there forever. Nothing needs a new branch\n// for \"an image cannot end\" — the existing branch already means that.\n//\n// This file is concatenated into the injected screen by entry.js, so it must be\n// plain script text: no imports, no exports, no module syntax. It defines\n// `globalThis.__DSH_BOOT_ANIM_RENDERERS__` and the screen reads it.\n\n/* eslint-disable */\n;(function () {\n  'use strict'\n\n  /**\n   * Build a renderer for one pool entry.\n   *\n   * @param entry - `{ kind, src, name, model }` from a pool manifest.\n   * @param options - `{ loop, onDiagnostic }`.\n   *   `loop` is what the entry is FOR, not a property of the file: the boot clip\n   *   plays once because its END is the hand-off signal, while the screensaver loops\n   *   because it covers the screen for an unknown length of time. A renderer that\n   *   always looped would never let the screen hand over; one that never looped\n   *   would freeze the screensaver the moment its clip ran out.\n   * @returns a renderer, or undefined when the kind is unknown.\n   */\n  function create(entry, options) {\n    var kind = entry && entry.kind\n    var opts = options || {}\n    if (kind === 'video') return videoRenderer(entry, opts)\n    if (kind === 'image') return imageRenderer(entry)\n    if (kind === 'animated') return animatedRenderer(entry)\n    if (kind === 'live2d') return live2dRenderer(entry, opts)\n    return undefined\n  }\n\n  /** Call a callback at most once. */\n  function once(fn) {\n    var fired = false\n    return function () {\n      if (fired) return\n      fired = true\n      if (typeof fn === 'function') fn()\n    }\n  }\n\n  /* ---------------------------------------------------------------- video */\n\n  /**\n   * A video clip.\n   *\n   * The only kind with a real timeline, and therefore the only kind that can\n   * carry a tail dissolve or unlock sound. Its `duration` may be Infinity (a\n   * MediaRecorder WebM carries no duration metadata), which the screen already\n   * handles as \"unknown length\" — so that fact is reported faithfully here rather\n   * than papered over.\n   */\n  function videoRenderer(entry, options) {\n    var video = document.createElement('video')\n    video.className = 'dshba-media'\n    video.muted = true\n    video.playsInline = true\n    video.setAttribute('playsinline', '')\n    video.preload = 'auto'\n    // The loop flag is the DIFFERENCE between the two uses, and it has to be set\n    // before the source is assigned so the element's first play already honours it.\n    //\n    // A looping element never fires `ended`, which is exactly right for the\n    // screensaver (it has no end to report — it is dismissed by the user) and\n    // exactly wrong for the boot clip (whose end IS the hand-off signal).\n    video.loop = options.loop === true\n    video.src = entry.src\n\n    var shownCbs = []\n    var endedCbs = []\n\n    // \"A frame exists\" is not the same fact as \"play() resolved\": a resolved\n    // promise only means the element left the paused state. The screen depends on\n    // that distinction to disarm its watchdog at the right moment.\n    var fireShown = once(function () {\n      for (var i = 0; i < shownCbs.length; i += 1) shownCbs[i]()\n    })\n    function checkShown() {\n      if (video.readyState >= 2) fireShown()\n    }\n    video.addEventListener('loadeddata', checkShown)\n    video.addEventListener('canplay', checkShown)\n    if (typeof video.requestVideoFrameCallback === 'function') {\n      video.requestVideoFrameCallback(fireShown)\n    }\n    // Advancing time is the same fact reported by none of the above, and it is the\n    // case a MediaRecorder WebM lands in: it may never reach readyState 2 and yet\n    // be playing frames.\n    video.addEventListener('timeupdate', function () {\n      if (video.currentTime > 0) fireShown()\n    })\n    if (video.readyState >= 2) fireShown()\n\n    video.addEventListener('ended', function () {\n      for (var i = 0; i < endedCbs.length; i += 1) endedCbs[i]()\n    })\n\n    return {\n      kind: 'video',\n      el: function () { return video },\n      start: function () { return video.play() },\n      dispose: function () {\n        try { video.pause() } catch (error) { /* never started */ }\n        video.removeAttribute('src')\n        try { video.load() } catch (error) { /* detaching the source is best effort */ }\n      },\n      onShown: function (fn) { shownCbs.push(fn) },\n      onEnded: function (fn) { endedCbs.push(fn) },\n      duration: function () { return video.duration },\n      currentTime: function () { return video.currentTime },\n      isEnded: function () { return video.ended === true },\n      isPaused: function () { return video.paused === true },\n      hasAudio: function () { return true },\n      // A muted element is already silent, so the ramp has nothing to take down\n      // and the screen skips it.\n      setVolume: function (value) { video.volume = value },\n      getVolume: function () { return video.volume },\n      mute: function (value) { video.muted = value === true },\n      isMuted: function () { return video.muted === true },\n      // Only a video can stall, and only a video has a MediaError.\n      onStall: function (fn) {\n        video.addEventListener('stalled', fn)\n        video.addEventListener('waiting', fn)\n      },\n      onError: function (fn) {\n        video.addEventListener('error', function () { fn(video.error ? video.error.code : 0) }, { once: true })\n      },\n      mediaError: function () { return video.error ? video.error.code : 0 },\n      raw: video,\n    }\n  }\n\n  /* ---------------------------------------------------------------- image */\n\n  /**\n   * A still image.\n   *\n   * No timeline at all: it is \"shown\" as soon as it has decoded, it never ends,\n   * and it makes no sound. Every one of those is expressed by the ABSENCE of a\n   * method, which is what routes it through the screen's existing bounded-wait\n   * path instead of needing a branch of its own.\n   */\n  function imageRenderer(entry) {\n    var img = document.createElement('img')\n    img.className = 'dshba-media'\n    // `alt` is empty on purpose: the overlay is announced by its own aria-label,\n    // and a decorative image inside it should not add a second announcement.\n    img.alt = ''\n    img.decoding = 'async'\n\n    var shownCbs = []\n    var errorCbs = []\n    var fireShown = once(function () {\n      for (var i = 0; i < shownCbs.length; i += 1) shownCbs[i]()\n    })\n    img.addEventListener('load', fireShown)\n    img.addEventListener('error', function () {\n      for (var i = 0; i < errorCbs.length; i += 1) errorCbs[i](0)\n    })\n\n    img.src = entry.src\n    // A cached image is already complete when the handler is attached.\n    if (img.complete && img.naturalWidth > 0) fireShown()\n\n    return {\n      kind: 'image',\n      el: function () { return img },\n      // Nothing to start: the load already began. Resolving immediately keeps the\n      // screen's `start()` contract uniform.\n      start: function () { return undefined },\n      dispose: function () { img.removeAttribute('src') },\n      onShown: function (fn) { shownCbs.push(fn) },\n      // No `onEnded`: a still image never finishes, so the screen bounds it.\n      hasAudio: function () { return false },\n      onError: function (fn) { errorCbs.push(fn) },\n      raw: img,\n    }\n  }\n\n  /* ------------------------------------------------------ animated image */\n\n  /**\n   * An animated image (GIF / WebP).\n   *\n   * It loops by itself and has no API to observe or control: no duration, no end\n   * event, no currentTime. So it is reported as having no timeline, exactly like a\n   * still image — the difference between them is only that this one moves. That\n   * is also why a STILL `.webp` served under this kind is fine: it simply shows\n   * and sits there, which is what the bound it receives expects.\n   */\n  function animatedRenderer(entry) {\n    var base = imageRenderer(entry)\n    return {\n      kind: 'animated',\n      el: base.el,\n      start: base.start,\n      dispose: base.dispose,\n      onShown: base.onShown,\n      hasAudio: function () { return false },\n      onError: base.onError,\n      raw: base.raw,\n    }\n  }\n\n  /* ---------------------------------------------------------------- live2d */\n\n  /**\n   * A Live2D model, rendered through an ADAPTER.\n   *\n   * The Cubism runtime is not bundled with this plugin: it is proprietary, it is\n   * large, and it cannot be shipped inside a decorative boot screen. What ships is\n   * the SLOT. An adapter is a function that receives `{ modelUrl, canvas, onReady,\n   * onError }` and drives whatever runtime the user has installed; the plugin\n   * never sees the runtime's API, only the adapter's.\n   *\n   * With no adapter registered the renderer reports an error, and the screen moves\n   * on to the next entry. That is the honest outcome: a model nobody can render is\n   * a pool entry that does not play, which the screen already knows how to survive.\n   * It must NOT look like a hang, which is why this fails fast rather than waiting.\n   *\n   * The adapter contract is stated HERE, not in a separate document: the shape of\n   * the function and the optional handle are the body of this renderer below, and\n   * the general renderer contract at the top of this file says which methods a\n   * kind must answer and which it must leave ABSENT. `AGENTS.md` (\"The media-kind\n   * abstraction, and why the ABSENCES are the contract\") explains the other half:\n   * why a live2d entry deliberately has no `duration()` and no `onEnded()`, which\n   * is what routes it through the screen's \"unknown length\" bound.\n   *\n   * Installing one is a single assignment before the screen runs — put a function\n   * on `globalThis.__DSH_BOOT_ANIM_LIVE2D__` — and the settings card is where the\n   * user is told when that did not happen: `src/client.js` paints the 无适配器\n   * badge on a model row whose page has no adapter.\n   */\n  function live2dRenderer(entry, options) {\n    var adapter = globalThis.__DSH_BOOT_ANIM_LIVE2D__\n    var canvas = document.createElement('canvas')\n    canvas.className = 'dshba-media dshba-live2d'\n\n    var shownCbs = []\n    var errorCbs = []\n    var handle = null\n    var fireShown = once(function () {\n      for (var i = 0; i < shownCbs.length; i += 1) shownCbs[i]()\n    })\n    function fail(reason) {\n      if (options && typeof options.onDiagnostic === 'function') {\n        options.onDiagnostic('live2d:' + String(reason))\n      }\n      for (var i = 0; i < errorCbs.length; i += 1) errorCbs[i](0)\n    }\n\n    if (typeof adapter !== 'function') {\n      // Deferred by a tick so the screen has attached its error listener before\n      // this fires; otherwise the failure happens before anyone is listening and\n      // the entry looks like it simply never started.\n      globalThis.setTimeout(function () { fail('no-adapter') }, 0)\n    } else {\n      try {\n        handle = adapter({\n          modelUrl: entry.src,\n          canvas: canvas,\n          onReady: fireShown,\n          onError: fail,\n        })\n      } catch (error) {\n        globalThis.setTimeout(function () { fail(error && error.message ? error.message : 'adapter-threw') }, 0)\n      }\n    }\n\n    return {\n      kind: 'live2d',\n      el: function () { return canvas },\n      start: function () {\n        if (handle && typeof handle.start === 'function') return handle.start()\n        return undefined\n      },\n      dispose: function () {\n        if (handle && typeof handle.dispose === 'function') {\n          try { handle.dispose() } catch (error) { /* the adapter owns its own cleanup */ }\n        }\n      },\n      onShown: function (fn) { shownCbs.push(fn) },\n      // A model loops indefinitely: no end, so the screen bounds it in time.\n      hasAudio: function () { return false },\n      onError: function (fn) { errorCbs.push(fn) },\n      // Optional extras an adapter may implement, forwarded only when present.\n      setExpression: function (name) {\n        if (handle && typeof handle.setExpression === 'function') handle.setExpression(name)\n      },\n      raw: canvas,\n    }\n  }\n\n  globalThis.__DSH_BOOT_ANIM_RENDERERS__ = { create: create }\n})()\n"
    },

      "content": "// Lossless `moov`-to-front rewrite, in process.\n//\n// Why this file exists at all: the rewrite used to live only in the package's\n// `tools/faststart.mjs`, and `tools/` is NOT part of the published package — the\n// installed profile has no tools directory, so a button in the settings card has\n// nothing to shell out to. The transform below is copied from that tool rather\n// than reimplemented, including its refusal rules, because those rules are what\n// the tool's own suite proved on real clips: equal length, the media\n// payload bit-identical after `moov` is stripped out, the chunk-offset tables\n// shifted by exactly the layout's shift, and the result asserted to actually place\n// `moov` before `mdat` (checking the OUTPUT, not the plan — a plan that leaves\n// `moov` where it was passes every other proof, which is how this tool once wrote\n// byte-identical copies and reported success).\n//\n// It lives in `src/` rather than `lib/` because `lib/` is generated: `lib/client.js`\n// is build output, and a hand-written module does not belong beside it. `src/` is\n// also what the Host-side suites mirror — `verify/verify-entry.mjs` copies\n// `entry.js`, `package.json` and `src/` into a scratch directory and imports from\n// there, so a relative import of anything outside that set fails at link time.\n//\n// Nothing here runs unless the user presses the card's 优化 button. The plugin\n// never rewrites a clip on its own.\n\nimport { existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, renameSync, rmSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'\nimport { open } from 'node:fs/promises'\nimport { basename, extname, join } from 'node:path'\n\n/**\n * Ceiling for an in-place rewrite, in bytes.\n *\n * Not a technical limit: `remux` holds the whole file in memory and then builds a\n * second buffer of the same size, so the peak cost is about twice the clip. 100MB\n * keeps that bounded in a process that is also serving the UI. A clip above this\n * keeps its badge and is left alone.\n */\nexport const MAX_OPTIMIZE_BYTES = 100 * 1024 * 1024\n\n/** A refusal the route reports as a plain sentence rather than a crash. */\nfunction refusal(code, message) {\n  const error = new Error(message)\n  error.code = code\n  return error\n}\n\n/**\n * Walk the top-level box list of an mp4.\n * @param buffer - whole file.\n * @returns boxes in file order.\n */\nfunction topLevelBoxes(buffer) {\n  const boxes = []\n  let offset = 0\n  while (offset + 8 <= buffer.length) {\n    let size = buffer.readUInt32BE(offset)\n    const type = buffer.toString('latin1', offset + 4, offset + 8)\n    let header = 8\n    if (size === 1) {\n      // 64-bit size: the real length follows the type.\n      if (offset + 16 > buffer.length) break\n      const high = buffer.readUInt32BE(offset + 8)\n      const low = buffer.readUInt32BE(offset + 12)\n      size = high * 2 ** 32 + low\n      header = 16\n    } else if (size === 0) {\n      // Extends to end of file.\n      size = buffer.length - offset\n    }\n    if (size < header || offset + size > buffer.length) {\n      throw new Error(`malformed box ${type} at ${String(offset)} (size ${String(size)})`)\n    }\n    boxes.push({ type, start: offset, size, header, payload: offset + header })\n    offset += size\n  }\n  if (offset !== buffer.length) {\n    throw new Error(`trailing bytes: parsed ${String(offset)} of ${String(buffer.length)}`)\n  }\n  return boxes\n}\n\n/**\n * Locate every chunk-offset table inside the movie box.\n *\n * The scan is confined to `moov` because `stco` as a byte sequence can also occur\n * inside compressed `mdat` payload by chance; restricting it and then checking\n * that the box length matches its own entry count makes a false positive\n * essentially impossible.\n *\n * @param moov - the movie box bytes.\n * @returns absolute offsets (into the original file) of each table's payload.\n */\nfunction chunkOffsetTables(moov) {\n  const tables = []\n  const needle = Buffer.from('stco', 'latin1')\n  const wide = Buffer.from('co64', 'latin1')\n  for (const [marker, width] of [[needle, 4], [wide, 8]]) {\n    for (let at = moov.indexOf(marker); at >= 0; at = moov.indexOf(marker, at + 1)) {\n      const sizeAt = at - 4\n      if (sizeAt < 0) continue\n      const declared = moov.readUInt32BE(sizeAt)\n      if (at + 8 > moov.length) continue\n      const count = moov.readUInt32BE(at + 8)\n      if (declared !== 16 + width * count) continue\n      if (sizeAt + declared > moov.length) continue\n      tables.push({ type: marker.toString('latin1'), dataAt: at + 12, count, width })\n    }\n  }\n  return tables\n}\n\n/**\n * Decide the new top-level order and the byte shift applied to chunk offsets.\n * @param boxes - parsed top-level boxes.\n * @returns the planned layout.\n */\nfunction plan(boxes) {\n  const moovAt = boxes.findIndex(box => box.type === 'moov')\n  if (moovAt < 0) throw new Error('no moov box')\n  const moov = boxes[moovAt]\n  const mdatCount = boxes.filter(box => box.type === 'mdat').length\n  if (mdatCount > 1) throw new Error('multiple mdat boxes are not supported')\n  const moovIsFirst = moovAt === 0 || boxes.slice(0, moovAt).every(box => box.type !== 'mdat')\n  if (moovIsFirst) return { already: true }\n\n  // `moov` goes immediately after the first box (`ftyp`), which puts it in front\n  // of `mdat` — that is the entire point. See the module header for what the first\n  // version got wrong.\n  const withoutMoov = boxes.filter(box => box !== moov)\n  const insertAt = withoutMoov.findIndex(box => box.type === 'ftyp') + 1\n  const ordered = [\n    ...withoutMoov.slice(0, insertAt),\n    moov,\n    ...withoutMoov.slice(insertAt),\n  ]\n  const mdatAt = ordered.findIndex(box => box.type === 'mdat')\n  const moovOrder = ordered.findIndex(box => box.type === 'moov')\n  if (mdatAt >= 0 && moovOrder > mdatAt) {\n    throw new Error('planned layout leaves moov after mdat; refusing to write')\n  }\n\n  let cursor = 0\n  const placed = new Map()\n  for (const box of ordered) {\n    placed.set(box, cursor)\n    cursor += box.size\n  }\n  if (cursor !== boxes.reduce((sum, box) => sum + box.size, 0)) {\n    throw new Error('layout does not conserve length')\n  }\n  const mdat = boxes.find(box => box.type === 'mdat')\n  const shift = (placed.get(mdat) + mdat.header) - mdat.payload\n  if (mdat !== undefined && shift <= 0) {\n    throw new Error(`moov would not move (shift ${String(shift)}); refusing to write`)\n  }\n  return { already: false, moov, ordered, placed, shift, mdat }\n}\n\n/** Apply a byte shift to every entry of every chunk-offset table. */\nfunction patchOffsets(moovBytes, tables, shift) {\n  const out = Buffer.from(moovBytes)\n  for (const table of tables) {\n    for (let index = 0; index < table.count; index += 1) {\n      const at = table.dataAt + index * table.width\n      if (table.width === 4) {\n        const value = out.readUInt32BE(at)\n        const moved = value + shift\n        if (moved < 0 || moved > 0xffffffff) {\n          throw new Error('a 32-bit chunk offset overflowed; the file needs co64, use ffmpeg')\n        }\n        out.writeUInt32BE(moved, at)\n      } else {\n        // 64-bit arithmetic all the way, not through a Number: a co64 entry can name\n        // an offset above 2^53, which Number cannot represent exactly, and rounding it\n        // would corrupt the only index the file has.\n        out.writeBigUInt64BE(out.readBigUInt64BE(at) + BigInt(shift), at)\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  return out\n}\n\n/**\n * Rewrite one file into a staging directory.\n *\n * Same contract as the tool's own `remux`, including that nothing is written\n * unless `writeTo` is literally true — this half always passes true, and the\n * default keeps the \"report only\" behaviour from becoming an accident.\n * @param file - absolute path to the source clip.\n * @param target - directory the rewritten copy is written into.\n * @param writeTo - false reports without writing.\n * @returns a human-readable result line.\n */\nexport function remux(file, target, writeTo) {\n  const name = basename(file)\n  const buffer = readFileSync(file)\n  const boxes = topLevelBoxes(buffer)\n  const layout = plan(boxes)\n  if (layout.already) return `SKIP  ${name}: moov 已在最前，无需处理`\n\n  const moovBytes = buffer.subarray(layout.moov.start, layout.moov.start + layout.moov.size)\n  const tables = chunkOffsetTables(moovBytes)\n  if (tables.length === 0) throw new Error('no chunk offset table inside moov')\n  const patched = patchOffsets(moovBytes, tables, layout.shift)\n\n  const pieces = []\n  for (const box of layout.ordered) {\n    if (box === layout.moov) pieces.push(patched)\n    else pieces.push(buffer.subarray(box.start, box.start + box.size))\n  }\n  const output = Buffer.concat(pieces)\n  if (output.length !== buffer.length) {\n    throw new Error(`length changed: ${String(buffer.length)} -> ${String(output.length)}`)\n  }\n\n  // Lossless proof: removing `moov` from both files must leave the same bytes.\n  const strip = (bytes, boxList) => {\n    const parts = boxList.filter(box => box.type !== 'moov')\n      .map(box => bytes.subarray(box.start, box.start + box.size))\n    return Buffer.concat(parts)\n  }\n  const before = strip(buffer, boxes)\n  const after = strip(output, topLevelBoxes(output))\n  if (!before.equals(after)) throw new Error('media payload changed; refusing to write')\n\n  const outBoxes = topLevelBoxes(output)\n  const outMoov = outBoxes.findIndex(box => box.type === 'moov')\n  const outMdat = outBoxes.findIndex(box => box.type === 'mdat')\n  if (outMoov < 0 || (outMdat >= 0 && outMoov > outMdat)) {\n    throw new Error('output still places moov after mdat; refusing to write')\n  }\n\n  const moovStart = layout.placed.get(layout.moov)\n  const newMoov = output.subarray(moovStart, moovStart + patched.length)\n  const newTables = chunkOffsetTables(newMoov)\n  if (newTables.length !== tables.length) throw new Error('table count changed')\n  // The self-check reads each entry at ITS OWN width. This used to read 32 bits out of\n  // both sides no matter what `width` said, so every co64 file — 8 bytes per entry — was\n  // compared against a value assembled from two neighbouring entries' halves, never\n  // matched, and reported `entry N not shifted correctly`. The rewrite itself was fine\n  // and the original was restored, so the damage was a FAILED button on exactly the\n  // large clips that most need faststart, not a corrupted file.\n  //\n  // The comparison is done in BigInt on purpose: a co64 offset may legitimately exceed\n  // 2^53, where Number silently rounds and a \"match\" would be a coincidence.\n  const shift = BigInt(layout.shift)\n  for (let index = 0; index < tables.length; index += 1) {\n    const width = tables[index].width\n    const oldAt = tables[index].dataAt\n    const newAt = newTables[index].dataAt\n    for (let entry = 0; entry < tables[index].count; entry += 1) {\n      const at = entry * width\n      const was = width === 4\n        ? BigInt(moovBytes.readUInt32BE(oldAt + at))\n        : moovBytes.readBigUInt64BE(oldAt + at)\n      const now = width === 4\n        ? absolute path.\n * @returns true when `moov` comes first, false when `mdat` does, undefined when\n *   neither box is inside the window.\n */\nexport async function leadingBox(file) {\n  let handle\n  try {\n    handle = await open(file, 'r')\n    const head = Buffer.alloc(65536)\n    const { bytesRead } = await handle.read(head, 0, head.length, 0)\n    let offset = 0\n    while (offset + 8 <= bytesRead) {\n      const type = head.toString('latin1', offset + 4, offset + 8)\n      if (type === 'moov') return true\n      if (type === 'mdat') return false\n      const size = head.readUInt32BE(offset)\n      if (size < 8) break\n      offset += size\n    }\n    return undefined\n  } catch {\n    return undefined\n  } finally {\n    await handle?.close()\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Move one pool clip's index table to the front, in place.\n *\n * The original is moved into `backupDir` first and the rewritten file is renamed\n * into its place, so the pool path never holds a half-written file: a reader sees\n * either the old clip or the new one.       "content": "#!/bin/sh\n# uninstall.sh - remove dsh-boot-animation from a DSH profile (macOS / Linux).\n#\n# The inverse of install.sh, and the POSIX twin of uninstall.ps1: drop the patch\n# row this plugin appended, and remove the directory link it created. The package\n# directory itself is never deleted, and nothing else in the patch layer is\n# touched.\n#\n# Paths are derived the same way install.sh derives them, so this works on any\n# machine. ASCII-only on purpose, like the .ps1 pair.\n#\n# Usage:\n#   sh tools/uninstall.sh\n#   sh tools/uninstall.sh --profile desktop\n#   sh tools/uninstall.sh --dsh-home /home/me/.dsh --profile web\n\nset -u\nLC_ALL=C\nexport LC_ALL\n\nPLUGIN_NAME='dsh-boot-animation'\nPATCH_ID='boot-animation'\n\nsay() { printf '%s %s\\n' \"$(date '+%H:%M:%S')\" \"$*\"; }\nfail() { say \"FAILED: $*\"; exit 2; }\n\nusage() {\n  cat <<'EOF'\nusage: sh tools/uninstall.sh [options]\n\n  --dsh-home <dir>     DSH home (default: $DSH_HOME, else $HOME/.dsh)\n  --profile <name>     profile to remove it from (default: web; the desktop app\n                       runs `desktop`)\n  -h, --help           this text\nEOF\n}\n\nDSH_HOME_DIR=''\nPROFILE='web'\nwhile [ \"$#\" -gt 0 ]; do\n  case \"$1\" in\n    --dsh-home)\n      [ \"$#\" -ge 2 ] || fail '--dsh-home needs a value'\n      DSH_HOME_DIR=$2; shift 2 ;;\n    --profile)\n      [ \"$#\" -ge 2 ] || fail '--profile needs a value'\n      PROFILE=$2; shift 2 ;;\n    -h|--help)\n      usage; exit 0 ;;\n    *)\n      usage >&2; fail \"unknown argument '$1'\" ;;\n  esac\ndone\n\nif [ -z \"$DSH_HOME_DIR\" ]; then\n  if [ -n \"${DSH_HOME:-}\" ]; then\n    DSH_HOME_DIR=$DSH_HOME\n  elif [ -n \"${HOME:-}\" ]; then\n    DSH_HOME_DIR=$HOME/.dsh\n  else\n    fail 'cannot guess the DSH home; pass --dsh-home <dir>.'\n  fi\nfi\n[ -d \"$DSH_HOME_DIR\" ] || fail \"no DSH home at '$DSH_HOME_DIR'; pass --dsh-home <dir>.\"\nDSH_HOME_DIR=${DSH_HOME_DIR%/}\n\nPROFILE_DIR=\"$DSH_HOME_DIR/profiles/$PROFILE\"\nPATCH_FILE=\"$PROFILE_DIR/cordis.patch.yml\"\nLINK_PATH=\"$PROFILE_DIR/node_modules/$PLUGIN_NAME\"\nSTAMP=$(date '+%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')\nBACKUP=\"$DSH_HOME_DIR/.dsh-rollback-$PLUGIN_NAME-undo-$STAMP\"\n\nsay '=== 0/3 preconditions ==='\nsay \"  dsh home: $DSH_HOME_DIR\"\nsay \"  profile : $PROFILE_DIR\"\nif [ !
